sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Jayadratha-vadha Parva, Section CXLII

verification.notes: Section CXLII: Satyaki, with his sword, cut off the head of the Kuru warrior who had been deprived of his arm by Partha and who was then sitting in Praya.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Jayadratha-vadha Parva, Section CXLII

verification.notes: Section CXLII: Satyaki beheads Bhurisravas with his sword as the armless warrior sits in the Praya vow.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Jayadratha-vadha Parva, Section CXLIII

verification.notes: Section CXLIII: Somadatta subsequently obtained the highly charitable Bhurisravas for son, in consequence of the boon he had been granted.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Jayadratha-vadha Parva, Section CXLII

verification.notes: Section CXLII: Arjuna, unseen, cuts off the sword-bearing arm of Bhurisravas to save Satyaki, and Bhurisravas rebukes him for the deed.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Jayadratha-vadha Parva, Sections CXLI-CXLIII

verification.notes: Sections CXLI-CXLIII narrate the duel of Bhurisravas with Satyaki, the loss of his arm to Arjuna and his death.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Ambopakhyana Parva, Section CLXXIV

verification.notes: Section CLXXIV names three maidens, daughters of the ruler of Kasi, Amva, Amvika and Amvalika; Amba is the eldest.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Ambopakhyana Parva, Section CLXXIV

verification.notes: Section CLXXIV: Amba, Ambika and Ambalika are the three daughters of the king of Kasi; Ambalika is the youngest.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Ambopakhyana Parva, Section CLXXVI

verification.notes: Section CLXXVI: Amba tells Salwa she had given her heart to him alone, and Salwa rejects her like a snake casting off his slough.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Ambopakhyana Parva, Section CLXXX

verification.notes: Section CLXXX: Amba begs Rama to slay in battle that Bhishma, vowing vengeance for her abduction from the svayamvara at Kasi.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Ambopakhyana Parva, Section CLXXIX

verification.notes: Section CLXXIX: Amba approaches Rama of Bhrigu's race, worships his feet with her bent head and seeks his protection against Bhishma.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Ambopakhyana Parva, Section CLXXIX

verification.notes: Section CLXXIX: the sage Akritavrana counsels Amba that her vengeance should fall upon Bhishma and no other.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Ambopakhyana Parva, Section CXCV

verification.notes: Section CXCV: it was the eldest daughter of the ruler of Kasi, celebrated by the name of Amva, who was born in Drupada's line as Sikhandin.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Ambopakhyana Parva, Sections CLXXIV-CXCV

verification.notes: The Ambopakhyana Parva recounts Amba's abduction, rejection by Salwa, austerities and rebirth as Sikhandin.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXXXIV

verification.notes: Section CXXXIV: Drona asks Ekalavya, if thou art really my pupil, give me then my fees, and demands the thumb of his right hand.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXXXIV

verification.notes: Section CXXXIV introduces Ekalavya, son of Hiranyadhanus king of the Nishadas, and narrates the guru-dakshina of his thumb.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Abhimanyu-vadha Parva, Section XXVIII

verification.notes: Section XXVIII opens: Having slain Bhagadatta who was ever the favourite and friend of Indra and who was possessed of great energy, Partha circumambulated him.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Abhimanyu-vadha Parva, Section XXVIII

verification.notes: Section XXVII narrates the duel of Arjuna with the ruler of the Pragjyotishas; Section XXVIII states Partha had slain Bhagadatta.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Abhimanyu-vadha Parva, Section XXVIII

verification.notes: Section XXVIII calls Bhagadatta ever the favourite and friend of Indra.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Mausala Parva, Section 3

verification.notes: Mausala Parva 3: Having said these words, Satyaki rushed at Kritavarma and severed his head with a sword in the very sight of Keshava.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Mausala Parva, Section 3

verification.notes: Mausala Parva 3: Satyaki beheads Kritavarma during the drunken quarrel, after taunting him for the night-slaughter of the sleeping camp.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Sauptika Parva, Section I

verification.notes: Section I: Kritavarma, Kripa and Drona's son alone survive the day's fighting and sit down together in the forest at nightfall.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Sauptika Parva, Section I

verification.notes: Section I: the two great car-warriors, Kripa and Kritavarma, succumbed to sleep beside Ashwatthama in the forest.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXXXI

verification.notes: Section CXXXI: Drona married Kripi, the daughter of Saradwat and twin sister of Kripa, making Kripa his brother-in-law.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Sauptika Parva, Section I

verification.notes: Section I: Kripa is the constant companion of Drona's son Ashwatthama, his nephew, among the three survivors of the war.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Sauptika Parva, Section I

verification.notes: Section I: Kripa and Kritavarma rest together with Ashwatthama in the forest after the fall of Duryodhana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Sections CXXIX-CXXX

verification.notes: Sections CXXIX-CXXX narrate the birth of Kripa from Saradwat in a clump of heath and his teaching of arms to the Kuru princes.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bhishma Parva, Jambukhanda Nirmana Parva, Section II

verification.notes: Section II: Vyasa, that lord of boons, gives Sanjaya celestial vision so that he may narrate the battle to Dhritarashtra.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bhagavadgita, Chapter I and Chapter XVIII

verification.notes: Sanjaya speaks the frame of the Gita: Chapter I opens with the question of Dhritarashtra to him, and at XVIII he says, Thus did I hear this dialogue between Vasudeva and the high-minded son of Pritha.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bhishma Parva, Jambukhanda Nirmana Parva, Section II

verification.notes: Sanjaya is the narrator of the war Parvas, reporting the battle to the blind Dhritarashtra by the boon of Vyasa.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Draupadi-harana Parva, Section CCCVII

verification.notes: Section CCCVII: a Suta named Adhiratha, who was a friend of Dhritarashtra, came to the river Ganga, accompanied by his wife.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Bhagavat-Yana Parva, Section CXLI

verification.notes: Section CXLI: Karna tells Krishna that Adhiratha of the Suta class regardeth me as a son, and I too, from affection, always regard him as my father.
